entries.206bf3e05b30d4b3: Revenue in the fiscal year ended February 2026 was ¥542,122 million. The way sales are recorded differs by the form of the work. For product sales in Motion Control and Robotics, revenue is recognized "at the point when products are delivered to the customer or accepted by the customer," and payment is received mainly within 4 months for Motion Control and mainly within 5 months for Robotics. On the other hand, contract work and the like in Robotics and System Engineering involves building equipment to customer specifications over a long period, so revenue is recorded little by little over the period according to the pattern of cost occurrence. Maintenance contracts are different again: revenue is recognized evenly over the contract period. Because the annual securities report states that "there are many products that do not take a make-to-order form, and production scale and order scale by segment are not shown in monetary amounts or quantities," order figures are not disclosed.

entries.2f8b76d9548ee7f1: Operating profit in the fiscal year ended February 2026 was ¥47,307 million, and the operating profit margin was 8.7%. Operating profit by business was ¥24,384 million for Motion Control, ¥20,418 million for Robotics, ¥4,989 million for System Engineering, and ¥1,988 million for Other. Although Robotics exceeded Motion Control in revenue, Motion Control exceeded Robotics in operating profit, so the rankings are reversed. The company explains that Robotics increased revenue through large projects in China and Asia but decreased profit "due to the impact of the added value of large projects," while Motion Control, despite lower revenue, increased profit year on year "due to improvements in added value and other factors." This means that even within the same company, the way of making money differs between a business that sells large volumes cheaply and a business that sells high-value-added components. Company-wide operating profit decreased from the previous fiscal year: although added value increased with higher sales, it could not cover foreign exchange effects and increased indirect costs.

entries.39359c889cbe9a4c: This business designs and delivers large electrical systems that run entire factories and infrastructure. The securities report states, “We are engaged in the development, manufacture, sale and maintenance services of industrial automation drives and social systems.” Its main work is taking charge of entire equipment rather than individual components, such as electrical systems for steel plants, electrical systems for water and sewerage systems and electrical systems for port cargo handling; it also handles high-voltage inverters, high-voltage matrix converters, industrial motors and generators, and generators for small-scale hydropower. In the fiscal year ended February 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥38,744 million, operating profit was ¥4,989 million and the number of employees was 737, excluding 98 temporary employees; it is the smallest business of the 3 reportable segments. By region, revenue from external customers was only ¥32,673 million in Japan and ¥6,070 million in Asia excluding China, with no amounts recorded for the Americas, Europe or China. Its domestic focus differs greatly from the other 2 businesses, which generate most of their revenue overseas. The company explains that sales to steel plants and social systems remained firm, resulting in higher revenue, and that profit increased due to the increase in profit accompanying higher sales and improved value added.

entries.daece8ead7bcdce9: At the root are motors and the technology of how to move motors. The report states that this company proposed the word “mechatronics (a coined word fusing mechanism and electronics)” in 1969. The same technology is sold in three forms. AC servo motors, which stop accurately at the instructed angle, and inverters, which freely change the rotation speed of motors, are components incorporated into machines. Industrial robots combine those motors into many arms and perform welding, painting and transportation. And electrical systems for steel plants and for water supply and sewerage are motors and control devices enlarged to the scale of facilities.
entries.dde4120616f4d9f3: It consists of YASKAWA Electric Corporation, headquartered in Yahatanishi Ward, Kitakyushu City, and 66 subsidiaries and 13 affiliated companies (as of February 28, 2026). The number of employees is 12,483, and there are also 1,879 temporary employees on an annual average basis. The organization is divided by business rather than by region, and the annual securities report states: "The organization is structured around 3 business units — Motion Control, Robotics, and System Engineering — and each business unit formulates comprehensive strategies for Japan and overseas and carries out business activities." Overseas companies such as Yaskawa America, Inc., Yaskawa Europe GmbH, and Yaskawa Electric (China) Co., Ltd. are companies that handle manufacturing and sales by region rather than by business. Its fiscal year ending at the end of February is also an unusual form among Japanese manufacturers, many of which have March fiscal year-ends.

entries.e7203f44586a4596: This business makes parts for moving machines at the speed and to the position desired. The securities report states, “We are engaged in the development, manufacture, sale and maintenance services of AC servo motors, control devices and inverters,” and according to the company’s description, the business consists of 2 businesses: the AC Servo Motor and Controller Business and the Inverter Business. AC servo motors are motors that stop precisely at the commanded angle, and inverters are devices that freely vary the rotational speed of a motor; both are components that equipment makers build into their own machines. The company also handles linear motors, AC spindle motors for machine tools, PM motors, digital galvano scanners, power regenerative converters, matrix converters and power conditioners for solar power generation. In the fiscal year ended February 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥236,053 million, ranking second by revenue, but operating profit of ¥24,384 million was the largest of the 3 reportable segments. The number of employees was 4,975, excluding 867 temporary employees. By region, revenue from external customers was ¥90,221 million in the Americas, ¥58,335 million in Japan, ¥45,921 million in China, ¥21,291 million in Asia excluding China, and ¥20,284 million in Europe, the Middle East and Africa; with the Americas as the largest region, this is in contrast to the robot business. The company explains that, although revenue fell as a reaction to the normalization of order backlog pursued in the previous fiscal year, sales to the electronic components and machine tool markets were strong, driven by AI-related investment; demand conditions improved from the second half of the fiscal year, and profit increased due to improved value added.

entries.eee005c30865610e: This business manufactures and sells industrial robots that perform work in factories in place of people, and installs and maintains them. The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states, “We are engaged in the development, manufacture and sale of industrial robots and other products, as well as maintenance services.” Models are divided by application, such as welding, painting and handling parts, and the company offers arc welding robots, spot welding robots, painting robots, handling robots, sealing and cutting robots, deburring and polishing robots, clean and vacuum transfer robots for semiconductor and liquid crystal manufacturing equipment, human-collaborative robots that can work alongside people, and robots for biomedical applications, among others. For the fiscal year ended February 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥247,012 million, the largest of the three reportable segments; operating profit was ¥20,418 million; and the number of employees was 4,728 (excluding 335 temporary employees). By region, revenue from external customers was ¥68,108 million in China, ¥53,658 million in Asia excluding China, ¥47,861 million in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, ¥39,521 million in Japan and ¥37,861 million in the Americas, with China and Asia together accounting for nearly half of sales. The company explains that revenue increased because, although sales to automotive markets in Japan, the Americas and Europe declined, large projects in China and Asia and the capture of capital investment demand in general industrial fields globally grew, while operating profit fell due to the impact of value added in large projects.

entries.f7d31e439fa511dc: It sells one technology, “motors and their applications,” in three ways: a business that sells it as components, a business that sells it as equipment, and a business that undertakes it as a complete set of facilities. The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states: “For 110 years since its founding, it has maintained motors and their applications as its business domain, and has enhanced motion control, power conversion and robot technology.” The AC servo motors and inverters sold by Motion Control are components that equipment manufacturers incorporate into their own machines and use. The industrial robots sold by Robots are equipment that itself performs work. System Engineering is work that undertakes, as a whole, electrical equipment for steel plants and for water supply and sewerage, and the report explains about contract work, etc. that “because performance obligations are satisfied by manufacturing products, etc. based on customer specifications over a long period and providing them to customers, revenue is recognized according to the pattern in which costs are incurred.” Sales are not concentrated on 1 company, and the report states: “No information is stated because there is no external customer accounting for more than 10% of revenue in the consolidated statement of income among revenue from external customers.” Revenue in the fiscal year ended February 2026 was ¥542,122 million, and revenue from external customers by [[term:segment|segment]] was Robots ¥247,012 million, Motion Control ¥236,053 million, System Engineering ¥38,744 million, and Others, not included in the reporting segments, ¥20,311 million.
